## Paste a clip's attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take them.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The item is on when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.

If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.

## What travels

Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.

Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.

| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing |
| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |

:::caution
The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
:::

A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.

## What stays on the target

Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:

- its place on the timeline and its length
- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
- its transition
- its name and label
- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)

Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.

## Adjustment clips and qualifiers

A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.

## When a paste stops

Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error naming the clip and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.

| The target | Can't take |
| --- | --- |
| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
| A movie or still clip | Remove Background with its subject set to Foreground, which only an image clip can take |
| Any clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |

To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things the menu item can't. It can name which groups travel, so it can paste the sound alone and leave the picture settings. And with groups named, it can paste across a mixed selection without stopping, skipping any clip that can't take a group. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
import AppKit

/// The Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section (spec §11 GR-13, grading-2
/// G2-4), on adjustment clips only, after Adjustment: which of the pixels
/// behind the clip its grade reaches.
///
/// Per range two rows — its checkbox (Hue, Saturation, Luma) in the label
/// column then its strip (`RangeStripControl`), then three captioned fields
/// (Centre, Width, Soft in whole degrees; Low, High, Soft to two decimals) —
/// then Invert, then Blur (spec §11 GR-35: the house slider and field,
/// 0–100 %, one step "Qualifier Blur"), then Pick from Canvas and the Show
/// Selection switch, both sent to the editor as commands
/// (`EditorViewController+Qualifier.swift`, `+Seeing`). A checkbox writes
/// `{}` or `null` (one step named after the range); a strip drag is the live trio; a field one commit; each sends the
/// WHOLE range to every selected clip, the first clip's values being the
/// ones shown (the mixed badge says when the others differ). Every row
/// writes `video.qualifier`, so a keyed action marks them all as one key.
extension VideoPane {
    // MARK: Qualifier

    func qualifierSection() -> InspectorSection {
        let binding = self.binding
        func qualifier() -> ColorQualifier { binding.videoProps.qualifier }
        func ops(_ patch: ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp] {
            binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(qualifier: patch))
        }
        var rows: [NSView] = []
        for range in QualifierRange.allCases {
            rows += qualifierRows(range, read: qualifier, ops: ops)
        }
        rows.append(
            inspectorCheckRow(
                "Invert", binding, name: "Qualifier",
                read: { qualifier().invert },
                ops: { ops(ColorQualifierPatch(invert: $0)) },
                mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.invert } }))
        rows.append(
            inspectorValueRow(
                "Blur", binding, name: "Qualifier Blur", unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0,
                max: 100, quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
                read: { qualifier().blur * 100 },
                ops: { ops(ColorQualifierPatch(blur: $0 / 100)) },
                mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.blur } }))
        let pick = commandButton(
            "Pick from Canvas", #selector(EditorViewController.pickQualifier(_:)),
            toolTip: "Click the preview to centre the ranges on a colour (Esc cancels)")
        let show = OptionCheckboxControl(
            label: "Show Selection",
            read: { [weak self] in
                guard let key = self?.inspector?.document?.recipeKey else { return false }
                return RecipeSource.shared.options(for: key).selection != nil
            },
            write: { [weak self] _ in
                self?.inspector?.onCommand?(
                    #selector(EditorViewController.toggleShowSelection(_:)))
            },
            enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
        rows.append(inspectorButtonRow([pick, show]))
        return InspectorSection(
            id: "video.qualifier", title: "Qualifier",
            summary: { qualifier().summary },
            reset: { binding.apply("Qualifier", ops(.reset)) },
            differs: { !qualifier().isNeutral },
            defaultExpanded: false,
            rows: rows)
    }

    /// One range's two rows: the checkbox and the strip, then the fields.
    private func qualifierRows(
        _ range: QualifierRange, read: @escaping () -> ColorQualifier,
        ops: @escaping (ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp]
    ) -> [NSView] {
        let binding = self.binding
        let name = range.title
        func on() -> Bool { read().isOn(range) }
        let check = OptionCheckboxControl(
            label: name, read: on,
            write: { [weak binding] value in
                binding?.apply(name, ops(.toggle(range, value)))
            },
            enabled: { true },
            onEdit: { [weak binding] in binding?.edited() })
        check.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
        check.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorMetrics.labelWidth).isActive = true
        let strip = RangeStripControl(
            kind: range, read: read,
            begin: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveBegin() },
            update: { [weak binding] patch in binding?.liveUpdate(ops(patch)) },
            end: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveEnd(name) })
        let mixed: () -> Bool
        switch range {
        case .hue: mixed = { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.hue } }
        case .saturation: mixed = { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.saturation } }
        case .luma: mixed = { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.luma } }
        }
        let stripRow = inspectorRow(
            nil, [check, strip], mixed: mixed, binding: binding, writes: ops(.reset),
            default: InspectorRowDefault(
                name: name, differs: on, ops: { ops(.toggle(range, false)) }))
        let gutter = stripRow.gutter
        strip.keyed = { [weak gutter] in gutter?.isKeyed == true }
        return [stripRow, qualifierFields(range, read: read, ops: ops)]
    }

    /// The range's three captioned fields across one row.
    private func qualifierFields(
        _ range: QualifierRange, read: @escaping () -> ColorQualifier,
        ops: @escaping (ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp]
    ) -> NSView {
        let binding = self.binding
        let name = range.title
        func on() -> Bool { read().isOn(range) }
        typealias Field = (caption: String, max: Double, get: (ColorQualifier) -> Double,
                           put: (ColorQualifier, Double) -> ColorQualifierPatch)
        let fields: [Field]
        if range == .hue {
            func hue(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierHue { q.hue ?? .initial }
            fields = [
                ("Centre", 360, { hue($0).center },
                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.center = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
                ("Width", 360, { hue($0).width },
                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.width = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
                ("Soft", 180, { hue($0).softness },
                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.softness = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
            ]
        } else {
            func levels(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierLevels { q.levels(range) ?? .initial }
            fields = [
                ("Low", 1, { levels($0).low },
                 { q, v in
                     var l = levels(q)
                     l.low = min(v, l.high)
                     return .levels(range, .set(l))
                 }),
                ("High", 1, { levels($0).high },
            let dim: CGFloat = chosen >= 1 ? 0 : (chosen > 0 ? 0.3 : 0.6)
            if dim > 0 {
                NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(dim).setFill()
                cell.fill(using: .sourceOver)
            }
        }
        DS.border.setStroke()
        NSBezierPath(rect: strip.insetBy(dx: -0.5, dy: -0.5)).stroke()
        guard isOn else { return }
        let isKeyed = keyed()
        let mark = isKeyed ? DS.action : DS.textStrong
        if isKeyed, let band = bandRect(in: strip) {
            DS.action.setStroke()
            NSBezierPath(rect: band.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5)).stroke()
        }
        for (handle, value) in handles() {
            for at in xs(of: value) {
                let size = handle == .low || handle == .high
                    ? Self.knob : NSSize(width: Self.square, height: Self.square)
                let box = backingAlignedRect(
                    NSRect(x: at - size.width / 2, y: bounds.midY - size.height / 2,
                           width: size.width, height: size.height),
                    options: .alignAllEdgesNearest)
                mark.setFill()
                box.fill()
                if size.width == Self.square {
                    DS.chromeBackground.setStroke()
                    NSBezierPath(rect: box.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5)).stroke()
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// The fully selected band's rectangle, when it does not wrap.
    private func bandRect(in strip: NSRect) -> NSRect? {
        let edges = handles().filter { $0.0 == .low || $0.0 == .high }.map(\.1)
        guard edges.count == 2, let lo = edges.min(), let hi = edges.max(),
            kind != .hue || (lo >= 0 && hi <= 360)
        else { return nil }
        return NSRect(x: x(of: lo), y: strip.minY, width: max(x(of: hi) - x(of: lo), 1),
                      height: strip.height)
    }
}

title: Set what an action animates to
description: With an action selected, use the Clip tab or the canvas to set where a clip ends up, read the marks that show what the action changes, and take a property back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip towards its end state: the values the clip reaches when the action finishes. A new action has an empty end state, so it changes nothing until you say what it animates to.

<AtAGlance
  where={[
    'Clip tab, with an action selected',
    'The canvas, with an action selected',
    'Right-click a row in the Clip tab',
  ]}
  tools="set_action_end"
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Actions header reads editing 1. The Graphic sub-tab shows a count of 3, and so does the Properties section, which has a Clear button. The accent, size and boxed rows each have a diamond in their left gutter. The size slider has a coloured fill and a coral tick, its field has a coloured border, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
/>

## Edit the end state

<Steps>

1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/). Clicking its band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing.

2. Change any row in the Clip tab. Type a value, drag a slider, pick from a pop-up or choose a colour.

3. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the clip travel to what you set.

</Steps>

While an action is selected, every field shows the value the clip reaches at the action's end, and every edit writes that value. Changing a row adds it to the action, and the row gets a ◆.

Your edits follow the selected action, not the playhead. If the playhead wanders out of the action's span, the action stays selected and the fields keep showing its end.

To edit the clip itself again, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane.

What happens along the way depends on the kind of value. Numbers and most colours ramp along the action's curve, and switches, pop-ups and text hold and then change at the end. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Edit on the canvas

With an action selected, the canvas writes the end state too. Moving, scaling, rotating or cropping the clip, nudging it with the arrow keys, dragging a text clip's wrap width and dragging an obscure region all change that action's end, not the clip.

The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead, while a drag starts from the end state and changes it by the distance you drag. With the playhead partway through the action, the box moves only part of the way. Work with the playhead at the action's end, which is where clicking the band puts it, and the box lands where you let go.

Two things on the canvas always edit the clip itself:

- A drag on a multi-clip selection. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- Resizing a shape's box, or dragging a line's or arrow's end points. A shape's own properties can't animate. Moving a shape still writes the action's end.

## Switch a property off

Untick a switch inside an action and that property turns off when the action ends. **Drop shadow**, a text clip's **Outline** and **Backdrop**, and sound switches such as **Limit peaks** all work this way, and so does a single band of the EQ.

The property stays on through the action, then goes off as it ends. The row shows ◆ and "at end".

This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.

## Read the row marks

Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.

| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ◆ | This action animates the row. | The label turns strong, and a field or pop-up gets a border in the action colour. |
| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates the row. | Its tooltip reads "Changed by action N". |
| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates. **Gain** follows **Volume**, for example. | |
| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row, so an edit here changes the clip. | The label turns faint. |

With an action selected, a blank gutter beside a control means it can animate and nothing is animating it yet.

◇ also shows when no action is selected, on every row an action on the clip animates. It's a quick way to see what's moving before you pick an action.

The **Normalize** button changes the clip whatever is selected. While an action is selected it carries a small boxed **clip** tag, and its tooltip reads "Actions don't animate this. It changes the clip."

### The "at end" tag

A control that can't blend says "at end" beside it once the action animates it. It holds its old value until the action ends, then switches.

Pop-ups, checkboxes, segmented controls and text fields all work this way. Most colours ramp, but a few can't blend, such as a cursor's ripple colour, and those say "at end" too.

## See the value change as it plays

The field always reads the value at the action's end. The rest of the row shows how it gets there.

**On a slider**, the rail fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. A coral tick marks the value at the playhead. The tick shows whenever the playhead is inside the clip and that value differs from the knob, even with no action selected.

**On a row with no slider**, a coral tag gives that value in words, such as "now 1.50×". It shows while the playhead is inside the clip and the value there differs from the field.

## Read the sections and sub-tabs

Section headers carry the same marks as their rows:

- **◆N** counts what the selected action animates in that section.
- **◇** means another action animates a row in the section.
- **⊘** means every row in the section is ⊘, and the section also says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."

The summary at the right of a header turns the action colour when the action animates the section.

### Sub-tab counts

Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N things on it, so you can see what an action does without opening every tab.

| Sub-tab | What counts |
| --- | --- |
| Picture | Each property. A zoom action reads ◆3, for its scale and its two position values. |
| Color | Light and Color together count as one. Look, Wheels, Curves and Qualifier count as one each, however many values inside them change. On an adjustment clip, Strength counts as one too. |
| Sound | Each property. |
| Text | Each property. |
| Graphic | Each property the action animates. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/). |
| Clip | A speed change, as ◆1. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). |
| Shape | Nothing, ever. A shape's own properties can't animate. |

### Sections open by themselves

Selecting an action opens the sections it animates on the sub-tab you're looking at, and they stay open for as long as that action is selected. A sub-tab you switch to later opens its own animated sections the first time it shows.

Close one by hand and it stays closed while that action is selected. None of this changes your own layout: leave the action and the sections go back to how you had them.

## Take a property out of the action

Taking a property out stops the action changing it. The row falls back to what the clip held before the action, and the action itself stays.

| To take out | Do this | Undo step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One row | Hover over its ◆ and click the × that replaces it. The tooltip reads "Remove from action N". | Remove from Action |
| One row | Right-click it and choose **Remove from action N**. | Remove from Action |
| A whole section | Click **Clear** in the section's header. Its tooltip reads "Remove this section from action N". | Clear |
| Everything | [Remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action). | Remove Action |

### Clear and Reset

**Clear** and **Reset** share one place in a section's header, and at most one of them shows.

- While an action is selected, a section with rows that can animate shows **Clear** if the action animates anything in it, and neither button if it doesn't.
- A section of ⊘ rows keeps **Reset**, because its edits go to the clip.
- With no action selected, **Reset** shows only while the section differs from its defaults.

## Right-click a row

Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.

| Item | When it shows | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove from action N** | The selected action animates the row | Takes the row out of the action. |
| **Go to action M** | The row shows ◇ | Selects the action that animates the row, and moves the playhead to that action's end. |
| **Set end value to default** | An action is selected, and the row can animate | Sets the value at the action's end to the row's default. |
| **Reset to default** | Any other row with a default | Puts the row back to its default. |

The two default items are greyed while the row already holds its default.

**Set end value to default** and **Remove from action N** aren't the same. The first makes the clip animate to the default. The second stops the action touching the row.

## Good to know

- Typing the number a field already shows isn't an edit, so it doesn't add the row to the action.
- Some rows always change the clip, whatever is selected, and they're marked ⊘. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) lists them.
- Adding or removing a filter or an obscure region changes the clip even inside an action, though dialling a value inside one animates. If the action already animates that list, the whole list then switches at the action's end rather than ramping.
- With several clips selected, the fields edit the clips themselves. The action lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
- An end value Frame Job won't take shows the reason at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/motion/change-an-action/#when-an-edit-is-refused).
- Selecting an action isn't an undo step, but each change to its end state is.

## With an agent

`set_action_end` does what the fields do. It can also do one thing the fields can't: send a value past a row's usual range, which is only held to that range as the clip is drawn. A graphic's properties are the exception, and are checked when they're set. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

description: "STUB"

STUB

## Reset curves

To straighten one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat**. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.

To straighten all six channels, choose **Reset** in the section's header. It shows while a curve is changed, and it's one undo step. You can also right-click the plot and choose **Reset to default**.

## Curves inside an action

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a curve edit goes to the action's end, so the curve animates. Any two curves animate into each other, whatever their number of points, and so does a curve and a straight line.

The plot shows it in its own way: the action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour.

To animate a curve back to neutral, right-click a cell and choose its **Reset** item, or right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**. Each writes a straight curve to the action's end, for the channels that aren't already straight. The section's **Reset** isn't there while the action is selected. **Clear** takes its place once the action animates curves, and removes them from the action.

See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Good to know

With several clips selected, the plot shows the first clip's curves, and the row shows **mixed** when they differ. An edit gives every selected clip the curve you're editing, for that channel, and leaves their other channels alone.

---
title: "Vectorscope"
description: "Read the hues in a frame and how strong they are, spot a colour cast, check skin tones against the skin line, and zoom in on a low-saturation picture."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The vectorscope shows a frame's colour with its brightness taken away: which hues are in the picture and how strong they are. Use it to spot a colour cast, to check skin tones, and to see how far a grade has pushed saturation.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
  keys="⌃⌘W"
  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's pop-up ▸ Vectorscope"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

<Shot
  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel beside it. The bottom slot shows the Vectorscope, a near-black square with six labelled target boxes around it, R at the top, Mg top right, B right, Cy at the bottom, G bottom left and Yl left. A line runs from the centre cross up and to the left, and a thin white trace runs from the centre towards the B box, for the blue card in the picture. The 1×, 2× and 4× cells sit in the bottom-right corner, with 1× filled."
/>

## Open the vectorscope

Choose **View ▸ Scopes**. A new window opens the panel with **Waveform** on top and **Vectorscope** below. If a slot shows something else, pick **Vectorscope** from its pop-up. Both slots can show it, each at its own zoom. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.

## Read the trace

Every pixel in the frame lands somewhere on the square, and the white trace is all of them together.

- **The centre is no colour.** Greys, black and white all sit on the faint cross.
- **Distance from the centre is strength.** A pale colour stays close in, and a saturated one reaches out towards the edge.
- **Direction is hue.** The [targets](#the-targets) show which way each colour lies.
- **Brightness is how many pixels are there.** The scale is logarithmic, so a small patch of colour still shows up beside a large one.

The two axes are the colour-difference signals: Cb runs across and Cr runs up. The scope draws no circles and shows no numbers, so the targets and the skin line are your only references.

A picture with no colour cast keeps its neutral areas on the cross. If something that should be grey sits to one side of it, the picture leans the way the trace leans. [Zoom in](#zoom-in-on-a-low-saturation-picture) to see a small cast.

## The targets

Six boxes mark where 75 % colour bars land, so you can tell which way a colour lies and how strong it is. Each label sits just outside its box.

| Label | Colour | Where it sits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R | Red | Up, a little left |
| Mg | Magenta | Up and right |
| B | Blue | Right, a little down |
| Cy | Cyan | Down, a little right |
| G | Green | Down and left |
| Yl | Yellow | Left, a little up |

## The skin line

The line from the centre to the edge, up and to the left, marks where skin tones fall. It's drawn at the hue of a standard light-skin reference colour, 123.3° counter-clockwise from the right.

Skin has a similar hue across complexions, and mostly differs in brightness and strength. If the trace from a face sits well to one side of the line, the picture has a cast.

## Zoom in on a low-saturation picture

The **1×**, **2×** and **4×** cells in the scope's bottom-right corner zoom in around the centre, to show small casts in a picture with little colour in it. Click a cell to choose it. The filled cell is the current zoom.

Frame Job counts the pixels again at each zoom instead of enlarging the picture of the trace, so a magnified trace stays sharp.

At 2× and 4×, a pixel too strong to fit on the square is left off, and it isn't piled up against the edge. At 1× everything fits.

All six targets are too far out to fit at 2× and 4×. Each one becomes a 6 pt tick on the rim that points towards it, with its label just inside.

Each slot keeps its own zoom when you pick another scope and come back, and when you hide the panel and show it again. A zoom lasts while the window is open. It isn't saved, and every slot starts at 1× in a new window. A cell works on the first click, even when its window isn't the active one.

## Good to know

- The scope measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values.
- In an HDR (HLG) project the caption reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and the targets and the skin line are redrawn for that colour space, with the skin line at 139.9°. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
- The scope is a 224 pt square. If the preview area is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them and stays square.

## With an agent

`render_frame` can measure a frame's vectorscope as numbers, at any of the three zooms. It says what share of the frame is neutral and, at 2× and 4×, what share lies off the plot, and it writes the counts to a file beside the image. It doesn't change a slot's zoom in the panel. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
- [Histogram](/color/histogram/)
- [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/)
- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)

---
title: "Histogram"
description: "See how a frame's tones are spread from black to white, and read how much of the picture is clipped at each end."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The histogram shows how a frame's tones are spread: how much of the picture is dark, how much is bright, and whether either end has run out of room. Use it to judge exposure and contrast, and to catch clipping while you grade.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
  keys="⌃⌘W"
  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's pop-up ▸ Histogram"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

## Open the histogram

Choose **View ▸ Scopes**, then pick **Histogram** from a slot's pop-up. Neither slot opens on it, because a new window starts with **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**. The choice lasts while the window is open. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.

## Read the histogram

Levels run from 0 on the left to 255 on the right, so black is at the left edge and white is at the right. The height at each level is how many pixels sit there.

Red, green and blue are drawn as translucent tinted fills, and luma, the picture's brightness, is a white line on top.

| What you see | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| A pile against the left edge | Shadows are crushed to black |
| A pile against the right edge | Highlights are clipped to white |
| Empty space at both ends | A flat picture, with room to add contrast in [Light](/color/light/) or [Curves](/color/curves/) |
| One colour's fill sitting to the side of the others | That channel is brighter or darker overall, which often means a colour cast |

Heights are on a logarithmic scale, so a small count still shows up beside a big one, and a peak twice as tall holds far more than twice the pixels. All four share one scale, set by the tallest count in any of them, so you can compare them directly.

## Clipping readouts

Two readouts sit below the histogram:

- **Highlights clipped** is the share of the frame at the very top level, 255.
- **Shadows clipped** is the share at the very bottom level, 0.

They read like "Highlights clipped 1.9 %", to one decimal place, and show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) shows the same two figures.

Both are measured on luma, so read them with these in mind:

- A single colour channel can clip while luma doesn't. Watch the fills at the right edge, or use the [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/), to catch that.
- They count the whole frame. Black canvas around a smaller picture, or letterbox bars, counts towards **Shadows clipped**.

## Good to know

- The histogram measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values. In an HDR (HLG) project it reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and luma is worked out for that colour space. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
- The histogram is 140 pt tall. If the preview area is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them.

## With an agent

`render_frame` can measure a frame's histogram as numbers. It says what share of the frame clips high and low by luma, and it writes the counts for red, green, blue and luma to a file beside the image. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## Related

- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
- [Light](/color/light/)
EOF

Two readouts sit below the histogram:

- **Highlights clipped** is the share of the frame at the very top level, 255.
- **Shadows clipped** is the share at the very bottom level, 0.

- A single colour channel can clip while luma doesn't. Watch the fills at the right edge, or use the [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/), to catch that.
- They count the whole frame. Black canvas around a smaller picture, or letterbox bars, counts towards **Shadows clipped**.

---
title: "Animate a grade"
description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every grade setting can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
/>

## Grade inside an action

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab.

3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from the clip's own value.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.

</Steps>

Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.

:::tip
An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
:::

## What ramps smoothly

These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's curve:

- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
- the look's **Amount**
- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**

## Curves animate

Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. A write to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.

| The two curves | How they animate |
| --- | --- |
| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |

### Animate a curve back to neutral

To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:

- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.

The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Curves](/color/curves/).

## A look switches instead

Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.

**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look with no action selected and set **Amount** to 0 %, then select an action and raise **Amount**.

The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.

## Animate a qualifier

A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.

### A qualifier range switches

Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.

If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.

An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.

### A hue centre takes the short way

An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.

## See what the action animates

Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.

- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.

The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:

- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
- Wheels
- Curves
- Look
- Qualifier
- Strength, when every selected clip is an adjustment clip

The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.

## Take a setting back out

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |

**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.

The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and pop-ups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.

:::caution
Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.
:::

## How each control shows an action

| Control | While the action animates it |
| --- | --- |
| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |

The coral marks show only when the value under the playhead differs from the end value. A qualifier's hue band that wraps past 0° gets its knobs in the action colour but no outline. The three wheels are one row, so all three discs and strips show these marks together.

## With an agent

An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the grade values for the action's end. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, and only **Amount** animates. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

---
title: "Copy a grade"
description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Copy', 'Edit ▸ Paste Attributes']}
  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
/>

## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take the grade.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.

## What comes with the grade

There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:

- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
- filters
- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them

A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.

:::caution
Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
:::

The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an action doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.

## LUTs travel with a paste

A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.

A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.

## A qualifier between clips

A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

## When a paste is refused

An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.

Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.

To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.

## With an agent

The menu item always copies every group of settings both clips have. An agent can name the groups it wants with `paste_attributes`, so it can bring the picture settings and leave the sound alone, or the reverse. The grade is still part of the picture group, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

Every grade setting can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
/>

## Grade inside an action

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab.

3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from the clip's own value.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.

</Steps>

Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.

:::tip
An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
:::

## What ramps smoothly

These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's curve:

- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
- the look's **Amount**
- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**

## Curves animate

Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.

| The two curves | How they animate |
| --- | --- |
| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |

### Animate a curve back to neutral

To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:

- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.

The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).

## A look switches instead

Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.

**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look and set **Amount** to 0 % with no action selected, then select an action and raise **Amount**. The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.

## Animate a qualifier

A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.

### A qualifier range switches

Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.

If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.

An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.

### A hue centre takes the short way

An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.

## See what the action animates

Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.

- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.

The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:

- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
- Wheels
- Curves
- Look
- Qualifier
- Strength, on an adjustment clip

The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.

## Take a setting back out

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |

**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.

The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and pop-ups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.

Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.

## How each control shows an action

| Control | While the action animates it |
| --- | --- |
| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |

## With an agent

An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the grade values for the action's end. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, and only **Amount** animates. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

---
title: "Copy a grade"
description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
/>

## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take the grade.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.

## What comes with the grade

There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:

- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
- filters
- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them

A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.

:::caution
Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
:::

The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an action doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.

## LUTs travel with a paste

A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.

A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.

## A qualifier between clips

A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

## When a paste is refused

An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.

Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.

To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.

## With an agent

The menu item always copies every group of settings both clips have. An agent can name the groups it wants with `paste_attributes`, so it can bring the picture settings and leave the sound alone, or the reverse. The grade is still part of the picture group, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)

---
title: "Animate a grade"
description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every grade setting can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
/>

## Grade inside an action

<Steps>

1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.

2. Open the **Color** sub-tab.

3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from the clip's own value.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.

</Steps>

Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).

While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.

:::tip
An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
:::

## What ramps smoothly

These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's curve:

- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
- the look's **Amount**
- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**

## Curves animate

Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.

| The two curves | How they animate |
| --- | --- |
| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |

### Animate a curve back to neutral

To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:

- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.

The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).

## A look switches instead

Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.

**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look and set **Amount** to 0 % with no action selected, then select an action and raise **Amount**. The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.

## Animate a qualifier

A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.

### A qualifier range switches

Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.

If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.

An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.

### A hue centre takes the short way

An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.

## See what the action animates

Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.

- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.

The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:

- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
- Wheels
- Curves
- Look
- Qualifier
- Strength, on an adjustment clip

The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.

## Take a setting back out

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |

**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.

The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and pop-ups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.

:::caution
Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.
:::

## How each control shows an action

| Control | While the action animates it |
| --- | --- |
| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |

The coral marks show only when the value under the playhead differs from the end value. A qualifier's hue band that wraps past 0° gets its knobs in the action colour but no outline. The three wheels are one row, so all three discs and strips show these marks together.

## With an agent

An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the grade values for the action's end. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, and only **Amount** animates. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)
- [Looks](/color/looks/)
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)

---
title: "Copy a grade"
description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
/>

## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take the grade.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.

## What comes with the grade

There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:

- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
- filters
- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them

A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.

:::caution
Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
:::

The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an action doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.

## LUTs travel with a paste

A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.

A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.

## A qualifier between clips

A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

## When a paste is refused

An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.

Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.

To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.

## With an agent

The menu item always copies every group of settings both clips have. An agent can name the groups it wants with `paste_attributes`, so it can bring the picture settings and leave the sound alone, or the reverse. The grade is still part of the picture group, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
